## Timing summary (descriptive)
n rows = 21; rows with both times derivable = 19; method: kill_recorded - claim_stated in minutes, only where both times are derivable and ordered; times are file mtimes (messages) or git commit times; mtime = last modification, commit time = commit not utterance, so durations are rough, may be inflated or deflated, and rows differ in kind (prior-art lookups, audits, measurements).
Durations (min): {'R01': 10.7, 'R02': 10.7, 'R03': 16.3, 'R04': 20.3, 'R05': 17.8, 'R07': 5.9, 'R08': 8.6, 'R09': 3.5, 'R10': 26.9, 'R11': 13.1, 'R12': 7.1, 'R13': 33.2, 'R14': 14.8, 'R15': 3.3, 'R16': 30.9, 'R18': 13.7, 'R19': 2.4, 'R20': 3.2, 'R21': 69.9}. Median over these 19 rows = 13.1 min (min 2.4, max 69.9). descriptive of THIS team on THIS day; not a rate, not generalisable; do not put the median on a slide without n and method and without the not-derivable rows.
Kill-type counts (prefix match): {'prior art': 7, 'counterexample': 1, 'measured': 4, 'mis-operationalised': 3, 'convention defect': 4, 'process defect': 1, 'design defect': 1}. Caught by an independent reviewer/validator/scout: 16 rows; mixed (author found it, independent hold also applied; R09, R15): 2 rows; by the author's own measurement or rule only (R17, R18, R20; all three are measurements, not reviews): 3 rows (no control arm; this supports 'independent audit caught what authors missed', not a collective-vs-single comparison).
